results.evidence: Five experiments addressed subcellular localization/trafficking of ENG p.Trp149Cys (W149C). Three studies (PMID: 10545596, 25080347) found functionally abnormal results: W149C is retained intracellularly and not at the membrane. Two experiments from a third study (PMID: 22022569) found functionally normal results: W149C traffics/matures similarly to wild-type. All used proper controls, but results are discordant.
results.reasoning: Eligible assays include cell surface biotinylation, pulse-chase, and subcellular localization (Step 2). Interpretable functionally abnormal results: (1) PMID: 10545596 (biotinylation, patient monocytes) show intracellular retention and reduced surface expression; (2) PMID: 25080347 (fluorescence microscopy in CHO-K1) also shows ER retention. Functionally normal results: PMID: 22022569 (confocal microscopy, EndoH assay) shows normal trafficking. These are different eligible assay types. Because there are at least two different eligible assay types showing functionally abnormal results, but at least two different eligible assays also show normal results without clear ambiguous experiments, the rule "with no clear contradictory result" is NOT met. Thus, conflicting results prevent application of PS3.

results.evidence: Six functional experiments were found for c.447G>C (ENG W149C): three subcellular localisation/trafficking assays (PMIDs: 22022569, 25080347), one endoglycosidase maturation assay (PMID: 22022569), one metabolic labeling/cell-surface biotinylation (PMID: 10545596), and a dimerisation assay (PMID: 25080347). Results are discordant: some trafficking/localisation assays (22022569) show normal localisation/maturation, while others (25080347, 10545596) report abnormal intracellular retention/loss of cell surface expression. Dimerisation was normal, but localisation of these dimers was abnormal. All experiments are eligible for BS3 as they assess trafficking/localisation or surface expression.
results.reasoning: Per rules, all trafficking/localisation experiments are counted as eligible for BS3. Among eligible experiments, at least two (PMID: 10545596, 25080347) report functionally abnormal results (intracellular retention, loss of surface expression, defective trafficking). Some assays (22022569) found normal trafficking/maturation, resulting in conflicting experimental results. According to the ACMG BS3 rule, if ANY eligible experiment is functionally abnormal, BS3 cannot be applied. Discordance between studies prevents application of BS3 even if some normal results exist. Dimerisation alone is not sufficient, especially since dimer localisation is still abnormal. No experiment is ambiguous by the definition—they are clear but discordant and must be combined as per rules. Therefore, BS3 does not apply.
